clue.text: Classes engaged in history and philosophy, say, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to be at something is to be engaged in it, as in 'at work'
history and philosophy are examples of arts subjects, flagged by 'say'

explanation.surface: Students from certain classes are taking courses in history and philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: AT plus ARTS gives ATARTS, which read backwards is STRATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers or levels of society, so the word is a synonym for social classes.

clue.text: Threaten to scrap unreliable car failing to start

indicators.note: a word that fails to start has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: to scrap something is to end it
a banger is British slang for an old, unreliable car

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to get rid of their clapped-out old car when it won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger, in British slang, is a battered old car; dropping its B leaves ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, which is what a threat does to it.

clue.text: Open global body had nothing to hide outside of negligence

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer pair of letters, the first and last
to hide something you wrap it up, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the United Nations is a worldwide organisation
someone who fasted ate nothing
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A world organisation went hungry to cover up its own carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' could be a verb here, but the answer is an adjective, a past participle describing something undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfastened, like a buckle or door, is no longer secured and so is open.

clue.text: What some hiker turns up for?

definitions.text: What some hiker turns up for?

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of them, a run of letters lying inside
in a down entry turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A wry question about why a rambler shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: KERT, hidden in hiKER Turns, reads TREK going up; and the whole clue is also the definition, since a hiker turns up for a trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A long walk or hike over rough country is exactly what a hiker sets out to do.

clue.text: A pop group holds record

indicators.note: something that holds another thing has it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: A-ha are a Norwegian pop band, known for 'Take On Me'
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A band is credited with holding a chart record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like an article, but it is the definition; the pop group is A-ha.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter and the radio code word for the letter A.

clue.text: Line for a drink reduced by 25% in ship

indicators.note: cutting a quarter off an eight-letter phrase removes two of its letters

blocks.note: a bar is where you go for a drink
a queue is a line of waiting people

explanation.surface: The queue for drinks aboard a ship has been cut down a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: BARQUEUE has eight letters; losing 25%, two letters from the end, leaves BARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a type of sailing vessel with three or more masts.

clue.text: Crumbs near pig full of energy

indicators.note: something full of another thing has it inside, so a letter goes into the word

blocks.note: by means near, as in 'stand by me'
to pig is to eat greedily, to gorge
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Breadcrumbs lie near an energetic pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' and 'pig' suggest food and farmyard, but crumbs is an exclamation and pig a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated British exclamations of mild surprise, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: Can I cut to boxing now, before match involving Everton finally?

definitions.note: the device speaking for itself; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so one piece goes inside another
finally points to the last letter of the word before it
something involving another thing takes it in

blocks.note: taken as written
in means fashionable, of the now
a peer is an equal, a match
the final letter of the football club's name

explanation.surface: A TV viewer asks to switch over to the boxing now, ahead of a football match featuring Everton.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English football club. The definition has the gadget asking to do its job, hence the question form.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is the kitchen tool whose sole job is cutting cans open, so it asks to cut one.

clue.text: Naked in back of strip club running drunken event

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
running suggests things in motion and out of place, so the letters are rearranged
one piece sits in the middle of the rest

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written, then rearranged
raw can mean bare or naked, as in 'in the raw'

explanation.surface: Someone runs nude round a strip club in a boozy night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip club' reads as one venue, but strip only gives its last letter and club is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a night of drinking that moves from one pub to the next.

clue.text: Dripping with the flavour of vegetable picked up

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio means heard, so the answer sounds like the wordplay

blocks.note: tasting of leeks, the onion-like vegetable

explanation.surface: A dish dripping with vegetable flavour, as a cook might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaky lets liquid escape, so it is dripping, like a faulty tap.

clue.text: Hot range of erotica gathered

indicators.note: of here means taken from part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A spicy collection of erotica has been assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron cooking stove, always warm.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga is a cast-iron kitchen stove that stays hot, and range is another name for such a stove.

clue.text: Articulate European lacking expression for 'complete freedom'

indicators.note: to articulate is to say clearly, so the answer is what the words sound like when spoken

blocks.note: a blank face lacks expression, and a Czech is a European

explanation.surface: A clever European has no phrase for total liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective, eloquent, but it is a verb telling you to say the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank cheque, signed with the amount left empty, is an idiom for unlimited licence to act.

clue.text: Problem-solving instructions oral might obscure

indicators.note: to obscure something is to blur it, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Spoken words might get in the way of a set of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure, like a recipe, that computers follow to solve a task.

clue.text: I'm about to trade whatever possible to get hold of cocaine variety

indicators.note: about as in about-turn means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
getting hold of something means taking it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
to trade goods is to sell them
C is slang for cocaine
any means whichever one might be

explanation.surface: A dealer admits being prepared to sell anything in order to buy cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellany is a mixed collection of assorted items, so it means a variety.

clue.text: Who lives for drink?

blocks.note: read as '...', someone who is, or exists
the familiar brewed alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A question about someone whose life revolves around alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks who lives for drink; split the answer as BE-ER, one who is, and it also means drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is ale or lager, an alcoholic drink brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: He's excited about Gold on television showing trailer

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround another piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
or is the heraldic word for gold
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A man is thrilled that a gold medallist is on TV, in a sneak preview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a film preview, but it is the vehicle; 'Gold on television' sounds like a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsebox is a trailer or van built for transporting horses by road.

clue.text: South Korean coins possibly obtained at great expense

blocks.note: coins are hard currency, metal rather than paper
the won is the currency of South Korea

explanation.surface: Some South Korean coins, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' admits the playful leap: coins are hard money, and the Korean unit is the won.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard-won was achieved only after great effort or cost.

clue.text: Senior judge and upper-class politician bound to compete in this

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the event

blocks.note: senior in rank means high-ranking
J is the abbreviation for judge
U is the abbreviation for upper class
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A senior judge and an aristocratic MP are obliged to enter a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it means a leap: you bound to compete in this event.
explanation.definitionFit: The high jump is an athletics event where competitors leap, or bound, over a raised bar.

clue.text: Dog that is pursuing Antarctic explorer

blocks.note: Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated expedition to the South Pole
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog chases after a polar explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pursuing means following, so the abbreviation is placed after the explorer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is the familiar short name for a Scottish terrier breed.

clue.text: Over DiCaprio, stopping affair later

definitions.note: a farewell, as in 'see you later'

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging a gap, so one piece fills the middle of another

blocks.note: over can mean excessively, too much
a do is a party or social affair
the actor Leonardo DiCaprio is known as Leo

explanation.surface: A story of someone getting over Leonardo DiCaprio after a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is easily taken as O; here it is TOO, and LEO plugs DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is an old-fashioned British goodbye, as casual as saying 'later' on parting.

clue.text: Briefly browse city

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to graze is to browse, as animals feeding on grass

explanation.surface: A quick look round a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Graz is the second-largest city in Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Graz is a major Austrian city, capital of the province of Styria.

clue.text: Pilot bothered by drills

indicators.note: drilling bores into something, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: as in 'what's eating you?', ate means troubled
via means by way of

explanation.surface: An airline pilot is annoyed by training drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drills' looks like a noun, training exercises, but it is a verb: VIA bores into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to fly an aircraft, which is what it means to pilot one.

clue.text: Formal sporting rules?

blocks.note: surface reading: the official regulations governing a sport
setter's reading: sporting means wearing, so these are rules on what to wear, with 'formal' one example

explanation.walkthrough: Sporting a tie means wearing it, and 'Formal' is a typical instruction on an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code sets out what clothes guests must wear, such as formal or smart casual.

clue.text: Retrospectively, Elon's beginning message on his platform?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the name
Elon Musk owns X, formerly Twitter, where messages are posts

explanation.surface: Looking back at something Elon Musk posted on his own social network.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex post is Latin for 'after the fact', describing something judged or applied looking back.

clue.text: Hammer small volcanic rock

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
tuff is rock formed from compacted volcanic ash

explanation.surface: A geologist takes a hammer to a little piece of volcanic rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like a tool, but it is a verb meaning to beat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs meaning to defeat an opponent soundly, as in a heavy sporting loss.

clue.text: You're not the only one to go to Chelsea?

definitions.note: a phrase for an action; the answer is the verb phrase

blocks.note: first meaning: a rueful phrase of shared suffering
second meaning: sign for a football team, Chelsea being a London club

explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea FC is a London football club, so a player going there literally signs up with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to someone complaining of a problem the speaker also shares, while signing for a team means becoming a member.

clue.text: Rejecting outsiders, members upset true selves

indicators.note: rejecting the outsiders means throwing out the first and last letters
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

blocks.note: legs are limbs, also called members
as in 'is that so?', so means true

explanation.surface: Turning away outsiders, club members are disturbed to show their real selves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True selves' reads as the definition, but true is wordplay; LEGS loses its outer letters to leave EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Egos are people's senses of self, the 'I' in each of them, so plural selves.

clue.text: Wash home of Hollywood lead from production

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, LA
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star finishes shooting and heads home to clean up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a leading actor in a film, but it picks out a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves lap or wash against a shore, so both verbs describe water moving gently.

clue.text: Design safety test with uncertainty

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in 'no ifs'

explanation.surface: A design passes its safety test, with some doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring pattern or decorative element in art or fabric, a design.

clue.text: Offensive old coach taking on negative football side beginning to object

indicators.note: a vehicle taking on passengers holds them inside
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a coach is a long-distance bus
no is the negative answer
a football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A veteran football coach takes on a negative team and starts to complain, rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a football manager, but it is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious behaviour is extremely unpleasant and objectionable, so it is offensive.
